entries.name: Scots pine
entries.leaves: evergreen needles, 2 per bundle, twisted, blue-green
entries.flowers: small yellow male cones and red female cones in spring
entries.fruit: small brown cones with winged seeds
entries.voxel_shape: tall straight reddish trunk, high sparse crown with flat top; lower trunk bare
entries.notes: The pine of the north: orange-barked upper trunk is unmistakable. Deadwood and snags are woodpecker territory.

entries.name: Norway spruce
entries.leaves: evergreen needles, single, four-angled, dark green
entries.flowers: purple male cones and green female cones, early summer
entries.fruit: long cylindrical hanging cones
entries.voxel_shape: dense conical crown to the ground; the classic Christmas tree
entries.notes: The dominant dark conifer of European taiga. Its resin once sealed boats; its boughs define the gloom of an old spruce forest.

entries.name: White spruce
entries.leaves: evergreen needles, single, stiff, blue-green with a sharp scent when crushed
entries.flowers: cones purple and green, late spring
entries.fruit: small slender cones
entries.fire: killed; shallow roots thrown over by wind too
entries.voxel_shape: narrow conical crown, thinner and more pointed than Norway spruce
entries.notes: The boreal workhorse of North America; First Nations and frontier builders split its straight poles for frames and sleds.

entries.name: Black spruce
entries.leaves: evergreen needles, single, short, blue-green
entries.flowers: small cones, late spring
entries.fruit: small cones, semi-serotinous (open after heat)
entries.fire: killed, but cones open after fire and reseed it
entries.voxel_shape: skinny short spire, often stunted and ragged on bog edges; dubbed 'drunken forest' when on permafrost
entries.notes: The bog spruce: stunted crowns, leaning trunks over muskeg. Fire resets whole stands — model it as fire-follower.

entries.name: Siberian larch
entries.leaves: needles in soft clusters of 20-40, fresh green, gold in autumn then shed
entries.flowers: red and yellow cones with the new needles
entries.fruit: small upright cones
entries.fire: survives (thick corky bark); fire-follower of the east
entries.voxel_shape: the only broadleaf-looking conifer: airy conical crown of soft lime-green, bare skeleton in winter
entries.notes: The great deciduous conifer of Siberia; turns a whole hillside gold in September then drops every needle.

entries.name: Downy birch
entries.leaves: deciduous, round-oval, slightly hairy twigs, yellow in autumn
entries.flowers: catkins before the leaves, spring
entries.fruit: tiny winged nutlets in papery catkins
entries.voxel_shape: slender pale trunk, drooping thin branches, a burst of green on a pale stem
entries.notes: The pioneer after fire and logging; pale bark and a light airy crown lighten any dark spruce wall.

entries.name: Paper birch
entries.leaves: deciduous, triangular-oval, double-toothed, gold in autumn
entries.flowers: catkins in spring
entries.fruit: small winged nutlets in cone-like catkins
entries.voxel_shape: chalky white peeling trunk with dark lenticels; high light canopy
entries.notes: The canoe birch: bark peels in wide waterproof sheets. A player who learns to peel it should get a crafting win.

entries.name: Quaking aspen
entries.leaves: deciduous, round with a fine point, flat-sided stalk so every leaf trembles; gold and red in autumn
entries.flowers: catkins before leaves, spring
entries.fruit: cottony wind-borne seed on female catkins
entries.fire: killed above ground; root clones resprout vigorously
entries.voxel_shape: pale greenish-white smooth trunk, rounded crown; whole stands flutter together in wind
entries.notes: One of Earth's largest organisms: whole clones connected by roots. The autumn 'tremble' is the forest's applause.

entries.name: European aspen
entries.leaves: deciduous, roundish, trembling on flattened stalks, bronze in autumn
entries.flowers: grey furry catkins before the leaves
entries.fruit: cottony wind-borne seed
entries.fire: killed above ground; resprouts from roots
entries.voxel_shape: tall columnar trunk, broad rounded crown; the bigger, longer-lived cousin of the quaking aspen
entries.notes: Shares the quaking-leaf trick with its American cousin; trunks split for log cabins with straightgrain.

entries.name: Balsam fir
entries.leaves: evergreen needles, single, flat with two white rows beneath, balsam-scented
entries.flowers: erect purple cones, spring
entries.fruit: upright cones that fall apart on the branch
entries.voxel_shape: perfect dense narrow cone with spire top; Christmas-tree silhouette
entries.notes: The balsam smell is the smell of the north woods; blisters on the bark burst with fragrant resin used as optical adhesive.

entries.name: Siberian stone pine
entries.leaves: evergreen needles, five per bundle, dark green
entries.flowers: cones with the young needles, early summer
entries.fruit: large egg-shaped closed cones of wingless 'cedar nuts'
entries.voxel_shape: massive broad-domed crown on a monumental trunk; the cathedral pine of old Siberian forest
entries.notes: A forest within a forest: nutcrackers cache its seeds and unplanted 'nutcracker groves' appear. The pine-nut harvest is a taiga economy.

entries.name: Rowan (European mountain ash)
entries.leaves: deciduous, pinnate with 9-15 leaflets, scarlet in autumn
entries.flowers: creamy-white flat sprays, late spring; smell mousey
entries.fruit: clusters of scarlet berries, autumn
entries.voxel_shape: small graceful tree, pinnate leaves, unmistakable bunches of orange-red beads
entries.notes: Planted by old farms as rowan for luck and protection; a red-beady beacon for migrating thrushes.

entries.name: Goat willow
entries.leaves: deciduous, oval with wavy margins, downy below
entries.flowers: furry 'pussy willow' catkins before the leaves, spring
entries.fruit: fluffy wind-borne seed capsules
entries.voxel_shape: bushy small tree; the source of the spring pussy-willow catkins
entries.notes: The pussy-willow: first food for bees in the cold north, and the branch the player should snap in March.

entries.name: Grey alder
entries.leaves: deciduous, oval, softly hairy, grey beneath
entries.flowers: long yellow male catkins, winter before leaf
entries.fruit: small woody cone-like catkins persisting through winter
entries.voxel_shape: slender grey-trunked tree by water, bare winter branches strung with little woody cones
entries.notes: Root nodules fix nitrogen, so alder thickets green up the worst ground; underwater it resists rot for centuries.

entries.name: Common juniper
entries.leaves: evergreen needle-scales in whorls of three, sharp, often bluish
entries.flowers: small cones, spring
entries.fruit: frosted blue 'berry' cones, take 2-3 years to ripen
entries.voxel_shape: low dense blue-green column or sprawl; dark prickly silhouette on open ground
entries.notes: The most widespread woody plant on Earth; frosted blue berries are the taiga equivalent of the desert's spice rack.

entries.name: Lingonberry (cowberry)
entries.leaves: evergreen, leathery, rolled-under margins, dark glossy green
entries.flowers: pink-white bells, late spring
entries.fruit: bright red tart berries, autumn
entries.fire: killed above ground; resprouts from rhizome
entries.voxel_shape: low evergreen mat of glossy leaves dotted with red beads
entries.notes: The taiga's cranberry substitute; Scandinavians eat it with everything. Easy low ground cover to paint a floor.

entries.name: Bilberry (whortleberry)
entries.leaves: deciduous, bright green, finely toothed, angular green twigs
entries.flowers: greenish-pink bells, spring
entries.fruit: dusty blue-black berries that stain fingers purple, late summer
entries.fire: killed above ground; resprouts from rhizome
entries.voxel_shape: knee-high twiggy bush, soft foliage; berry-stained ground beneath
entries.notes: European cousin of the blueberry with darker, more intense fruit; picking season is a Scandinavian institution.

entries.name: Bog bilberry (bog blueberry)
entries.leaves: deciduous, bluish-green, rolled edges, glaucous below
entries.flowers: pinkish bells, spring
entries.fruit: glaucous blue berries, sweet-bland compared with bilberry
entries.voxel_shape: low spreading shrub on wet bog ground, leaves a chalky blue-green
entries.notes: The bog blueberry: tougher and bluffer than the bilberry, happy in the same wet peat as cloudberry.

entries.name: European cranberry (small cranberry)
entries.leaves: evergreen, tiny, pointed, rolled margins, underside bluish
entries.flowers: nodding pink pull-back-petal bells, summer
entries.fruit: small dark red sour berries hanging from fine threads, late autumn
entries.voxel_shape: wiry creeping mat with tiny leaves and dangling red lanterns
entries.notes: Britain's wild cranberry: a string-and-bead vine over sphagnum; the cultivated bog cranberry is its American cousin.

entries.name: Cloudberry (bakeapple)
entries.leaves: deciduous, round-kidney, 5-7 shallow lobes, single per stem
entries.flowers: solitary white 5-petaled flower, male and female on separate plants; spring
entries.fruit: raspberry-like drupelets, red then amber, single per stem; late summer
entries.voxel_shape: one modest stem with one lobed leaf and one amber berry — the prize of the open bog
uses: preserve harvested by Sami and Inuit
entries.notes: Amber gold of the bog: each plant fruits one berry, and only if a male plant flowers nearby. A rare-berry find should feel earned.

entries.name: Bearberry (kinnikinnick)
entries.leaves: evergreen, small, leathery, rounded, dark glossy green
entries.flowers: small pink urn bells, spring
entries.fruit: mealy red berries, autumn; bear favourite
entries.voxel_shape: low evergreen creeping mat of small round leaves
entries.notes: Indigenous nations mixed its leaves with tobacco; the mealy red fruit is eaten by bears barely more than by birds.

entries.name: Black crowberry
entries.leaves: evergreen, needle-like in whorls, crowded along trailing stems
entries.flowers: tiny purplish or greenish, spring
entries.fruit: shiny black berries, mid-late summer, tart and dry
entries.voxel_shape: dark wiry ground-hugging carpet with crow-black beads
entries.notes: The berry that outlasts winter on the bush; bland but indestructible, long valued as a traveller's emergency ration.

entries.name: Heather (ling)
entries.leaves: evergreen, tiny scale-like overlapping along wiry stems
entries.flowers: dense spikes of pink to purple bells, late summer into autumn
entries.fruit: small dry capsules, inconspicuous
entries.fire: killed; seed regenerates on burned ground
entries.voxel_shape: purple-haze carpet, waist-low bloom in late September
entries.notes: Stripes the open pine heath purple in autumn; beekeepers prize single-hive heather honey.

entries.name: Bog Labrador tea
entries.leaves: evergreen, leathery, dark glossy above, rusty woolly felted beneath, intensely fragrant
entries.flowers: white cottony clusters, late spring
entries.fruit: small ovoid capsules in clusters
entries.voxel_shape: knee-high dark shrub with white bottlebrush heads, rusty underleaf flash in wind
entries.notes: Despite the name it is a rhododendron; the 'tea' can be harsh in quantity — a cautious bush should deter a careless player.

entries.name: Sweet gale (bog myrtle)
entries.leaves: deciduous, spoon-shaped with resinous dots, spicy-sweet when crushed
entries.flowers: small catkins before leaves, spring
entries.fruit: warty cone-like cluster of small nutlets
entries.voxel_shape: waist-high spicy thicket on wet ground near lakes and rivers
uses: seasoning for smoked salmon and eel
entries.notes: Rub the leaf on skin and mosquitoes lose interest; a natural midge net for a riverside campfire scene.

entries.name: Twinflower
entries.leaves: evergreen, tiny, rounded, paired, glossy
entries.flowers: two nodding pink bells per slender stalk, fragrant, early summer
entries.fruit: tiny dry single-seeded nutlet
entries.fire: killed; regenerates slowly from seed and rhizome
entries.voxel_shape: a whisper of paired pink bells at ankle height on old spruce moss carpet
uses: Linnaeus' namesake, living emblem of botany
no practical use — a wonder for walkers
entries.notes: Named and loved by Carl Linnaeus; two blush-pink bells on one wiry stalk. A perfect 'found it' moment for an observant player.

entries.name: Bunchberry (crackerberry)
entries.leaves: deciduous, whorled six leaves with strongly parallel side veins
entries.flowers: small green cross of florets inside four showy white bracts, like one big white dogwood flower
entries.fruit: tight bunch of scarlet berries, late summer
entries.fire: killed above ground; resprouts from rhizome
entries.voxel_shape: a doll-sized white flower that turns into a squeaky red berry bunch at ankle height
uses: the 'cracker' snap when the seed pops
entries.notes: A dogwood shrunk to ground cover; the white flower is a lie for ants, the red bunch is the reward for birds.

entries.name: Pipsissewa (prince's pine)
entries.leaves: evergreen, dark green, thick, waxy, finely spiny-toothed, in whorls
entries.flowers: nodding waxy pink-white umbrella clusters, mid-summer
entries.fruit: dry five-parted capsule, winter-persistent
entries.voxel_shape: small evergreen rosettes of wax-spined leaves, dollhouse blossoms in July
entries.notes: 'Pipsisikweu' = broken-into-small-pieces: chewed to ease kidney trouble; a plant to reward apothecary players.

entries.name: Sphagnum moss
entries.leaves: green to cherry-red branching moss in hummocks and hollows
entries.voxel_shape: springy cushion carpet, green to wine-red; holds many times its weight in water
entries.notes: The bog's architecture: builds peat a millimetre a year for millennia; squeezes clean antiseptic water when walked on.

entries.name: Reindeer lichen
entries.leaves: pale grey-green branching fruticose tufts, no true leaves
entries.voxel_shape: grey caribou antlers drawn on the ground by frost
uses: emergency water filter myth (bitter, low nutrition)
entries.notes: The ground a reindeer sees: vast pale mats it smells with its antler-adapted nose through the snow. Slow to regrow — fragile ground.

entries.name: Common bracken
entries.leaves: deciduous, large triangular three-pinnate fronds
entries.fruit: spore clusters on frond undersides in late summer
entries.fire: killed at surface; rhizome resprouts vigorously
entries.voxel_shape: shoulder-high eagles'-wing fronds in dense ranks
entries.notes: Beautiful and toxic-ish: ptaquiloside makes it carcinogenic when eaten raw. A dense patch can hide a crouching threat.

entries.name: Ostrich fern
entries.leaves: deciduous, vase-shaped crown of arching feather fronds; fertile fronds short and brown, persisting
entries.fruit: spores on fertile fronds
entries.voxel_shape: a green fountain jet of feathers on the stream bank
entries.notes: The edible fiddlehead: gather the unrolled croziers only; mature fronds and lookalikes are unsafe. Nice foraging beat for the player.

entries.name: Porcini (cep)
entries.fire: fruiting body killed; mycelium often survives
entries.voxel_shape: thick white-stemmed king with a glossy brown cap, tube sponge beneath, no gills
entries.notes: The king bolete: mycorrhizal with spruce, pine and birch; after rain in August the whole village goes looking.

entries.name: Chanterelle
entries.voxel_shape: a small golden funnel with blunt false gills running down the stem
entries.notes: Apricot-scented gold; the false chanterelle nearby is the lesson in lookalikes. Worm-free — a rare gift from the forest.

entries.name: Fly agaric
entries.fire: fruiting body killed; can reappear after fire
entries.voxel_shape: the storybook red cap with white warts and a white skirt on the stem
uses: not safe to eat; ibotenic acid toxin
Sami shamanic use historically (dried, with reindeer urine recycling)
entries.notes: The most famous mushroom alive; pretty, poisonous, and soaked in Siberian ritual. Render it beautifully and never forageable.

entries.name: Birch polypore (razor strop fungus)
entries.fire: killed; tree hosts usually die first anyway
entries.voxel_shape: smooth horseshoe-bracket on dead birch, grey-brown above, white below, 5-25 cm wide
entries.notes: Ötzi carried it 5300 years ago: one for tinder, one for medicine. A dead birch with brackets marks slow rot and good campfire fungus.

entries.name: False morel (brain gyromitra)
entries.fire: famously fruits on fire and logging ground after disturbance
entries.voxel_shape: a wrinkled reddish-brown brain on a short pale stem — unnervingly like a small cerebral cortex
uses: not edible raw; gyromitrin toxin metabolizes to a rocket-fuel chemical
legal food only after repeated boiling discards water (still risky)
entries.notes: Appears after fire — the taiga's post-burn warning sign. Anti-lesson mushroom: beautiful, fatal when mishandled.
